title: Ada: A Series of Collages

description.main: Announcement card for Jack Walls's 2008 exhibition of the Ada collages at Fuse Gallery, New York — the card front reproduces one of the works, a studio portrait sliced into crescent cuts. February 23 – March 22, 2008.
description.extended:
Ada: A Series of Collages is the announcement card for Jack Walls's 2008 exhibition at Fuse Gallery in the East Village — the Chicago-born artist's fine-art solo debut, mounted at fifty, of collages cut from imagery sourced from Robert Mapplethorpe, whose partner and muse Walls had been through the 1980s.

The 4 × 6 inch card fronts one of the Ada works: a black-and-white studio portrait of a young man sliced into rhythmic crescent cuts and remounted on a pale painted ground, the figure surfacing between the blades. The reverse carries the particulars — February 23 through March 22, 2008 at 93 Second Avenue, the gallery in the back room of Lit Lounge, with an opening reception on the 23rd and a video installation by Zachary Stuart-Pontier. The card comes from Gallery 98, the online archive of downtown New York art ephemera.

Walls met Mapplethorpe in the early 1980s and remained his partner and muse until the photographer's death in 1989, then built a practice of his own across writing, painting, and collage — and became an elder to the downtown generation of Ryan McGinley, Dan Colen, and Dash Snow. He lives and works in Hudson, New York. This is the first Jack Walls item in the library, filed with the collage collection's ephemera.
description.artist_bio: Jack Walls (b. Chicago; 1957 per his Vice interview, 1958 in some profiles) — artist, writer, and poet; partner and muse of Robert Mapplethorpe from the early 1980s until 1989. Works across painting, collage, drawing, and autobiographical writing (The Ebony Prick of the White Rose's Thorn); an influence on Ryan McGinley, Dan Colen, and Dash Snow. Lives and works in Hudson, NY. Official site jackwalls.com.
description.exhibition_context: Jack Walls: Ada: A Series of Collages, Fuse Gallery, 93 Second Avenue, New York, February 23 – March 22, 2008; opening reception February 23; video installation by Zachary Stuart-Pontier. Per a Threadless interview, Walls's first fine-art solo exhibition, featuring the Mapplethorpe-sourced Ada collages.

notes: Exhibition ephemera, not a book: gallery announcement card sourced from Gallery 98 (the user-provided listing), which dates and measures it (6 x 4 in). All exhibition particulars transcribed from the card back (scan on the listing): dates, address, reception, Zachary Stuart-Pontier video-installation credit. No ISBN — none exists for gallery cards. Fuse Gallery (in the back of Lit Lounge, 93 Second Ave) is long closed and fusegallerynyc.com is dead, so publisher_url points to the Gallery 98 item page. Walls's birth year conflicts across sources (1957 per his own Vice interview, 1958 elsewhere) — omitted from the description. Front-image collage description is from direct inspection of the card scan. Collage collection archiving, July 2026. Accessioned 2026-07-31.
